quote: Oh, no. No. We we can do that for you.
stewart_read: Rep answers a technical prewiring/electrical question definitively instead of deferring to the specialist, giving away appointment value on a non-standard build.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be reassuring on a simple point to keep momentum, not full scope creep — but the customer explicitly asks a technical build question the rep isn't positioned to guarantee.
coaching_implication: Use the escape hatch here: 'that's exactly what our specialist will confirm on site' instead of promising capability the rep can't verify.

quote: is it a garage on the property, or is it a separate garage?
stewart_read: A newly-built, meterless, detached garage is outside standard residential solar scope; this warranted a supervisor check or explicit non-standard flag rather than continuing the normal script.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have correctly judged this as within normal handling since Ion still sent a specialist; but no internal consult or explicit non-standard framing occurred.
coaching_implication: Flag detached/meterless structures for a quick hold-and-check before continuing normal qualification, since design implications differ from home solar.

quote: Is this your first time seeing this, design for the garage?
stewart_read: Customer's answer reveals a competitor name mention ('Thomann Solar') and intent to call other references, but rep doesn't probe what he saw or who else he's contacting.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be intentionally avoiding opening a competitive comparison this late in a short call to protect the booked time — but no evidence supports this as deliberate.
coaching_implication: Should have asked 'what did Thomann show you?' to surface competitive context before button-up.

quote: can you give me a can you give me a consensus of what it would take to have that minimal amount of solar up there?
stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a clear buying-intent signal (wants a rough sense of minimal system) but rep only redirects to the specialist without building curiosity or reinforcing the appointment's value.
alternative_hypothesis: Redirecting to specialist is the correct scope move; the miss is not doing it while also creating forward pull ('that's exactly the kind of number the design tomorrow will nail down for you').
coaching_implication: Pair the redirect with a curiosity hook tied to tomorrow's appointment rather than a flat deflection.

quote: have receptacles out there. Now I need to ask a question.
stewart_read: Customer is already imagining specific garage uses (power tools, lights, receptacles) — a strong buying signal the rep could have reflected back to build momentum.
coaching_implication: Rep should acknowledge and amplify this ('sounds like a great workshop setup — the specialist can size it exactly for that') rather than moving straight to address verification.

quote: then we got you all qualified. I have everything I need here on my side.
stewart_read: Rep declares full qualification while bill amount, interest reason, and co-owner status were all skipped per verified events, understating what's still unknown before the specialist visit.
alternative_hypothesis: For a garage-only, non-home system, some home-qualification items may be less relevant, but bill/interest are still core anchors regardless of structure.
coaching_implication: Do not claim full qualification when core verify items are missing; at minimum capture the bill or interest reason before button-up.
